definition: A unique numerical identifier assigned to every device connected to the internet, used to route data and identify your location and internet service provider.
metaDescription: Learn what an IP address is, how it reveals your location and identity online, and why it matters for your digital privacy and security.
simpleExplanation: Think of an IP address like your home's postal address, but for the internet. Every device online gets a unique number that tells websites and services where you're located and which internet company you use.
whyItMatters: Your IP address can reveal your approximate location, internet provider, and browsing habits to websites, advertisers, and potentially malicious actors. It's one of the primary ways you can be tracked online.
technicalDetail: IP addresses come in two versions: IPv4 (like 192.168.1.1) using 32-bit numbers, and IPv6 (like 2001:db8::1) using 128-bit numbers. They can be static (permanent) or dynamic (changing), and include both public addresses visible to the internet and private addresses used within local networks.

examples.explanation: When you visit a website, it automatically sees your IP address and can determine you're browsing from New York using Verizon, even if you don't provide this information.
Netflix shows different movies in different countries by checking your IP address location, which is why some content isn't available when you travel.
Ad networks use your IP address to show location-based ads, like promoting local restaurants or services in your city.
